newsitem.title: ITALY: SOCCER-INTER KNOCK JUVENTUS OUT OF ITALIAN CUP.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-INTER KNOCK JUVENTUS OUT OF ITALIAN CUP.

text.p: MILAN, Dec 18 (Reute) - Internazionale knocked Juventus out of the Italian Cup on Wednesday, holding the European champions to a 1-1 draw to reach the semifinals after gaining a 3-0 advantage in the first leg.
Inter take on Napoli in next month's semifinals and Vicenza face newly-promoted Bologna.

Juventus, who have soared to the top of the domestic league since winning the World Club Cup last month, put in yet another fine peformance despite the absence of top strikers Alessandro Del Piero and Alen Boksic.

It took a brilliant move by Inter's Paul Ince in the 50th minute to quash any fears that Juventus could make up the 3-0 gap after an elegant goal by Nicola Amoruso put the Turin club ahead just before the interval.
England international Ince won the ball in midfield and split Juve's defence with a pinpoint pass for Maurizio Ganz to blast a shot past Michelangelo Rampulla.

The equaliser induced a collective sigh of relief among the 15,000 fans Inter's San Siro stadium who had seen their side throw away a 3-1 lead in the last five minutes to lose 4-3 to Sampdoria last Sunday.
Juventus had been superior up till then, despite some good play by Inter, but Boksic's subsitute Michele Padovano wasted two fine chances and Amoruso sent a header high just before scoring.
Padovano set the goal up with a pass to Amoruso in the box after a perfect cross from veteran midfielder Attilio Lombardo, who has recently returned after a lengthy muscle injury.
Juventus, who won the Italian Cup in 1994, must now concentrate on their defence of the European Cup and winning the domestic league title.
